1	---
2	title: Tools
3	---
4	
5	<div id="enable-section-numbers" />
6	
7	The Model Context Protocol (MCP) allows servers to expose tools that can be invoked by
8	language models. Tools enable models to interact with external systems, such as querying
9	databases, calling APIs, or performing computations. Each tool is uniquely identified by
10	a name and includes metadata describing its schema.
11	
12	<Note>
13	  For brevity, the request examples on this page omit the `_meta` request
14	  metadata (`io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion`,
15	  `io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo`, and
16	  `io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities`). Every request **MUST** include
17	  the required `_meta` fields; see
18	  [`_meta`](/specification/2026-07-28/basic/index#meta).
19	</Note>
20	
21	## User Interaction Model
22	
23	Tools in MCP are designed to be **model-controlled**, meaning that the language model can
24	discover and invoke tools automatically based on its contextual understanding and the
25	user's prompts.
26	
27	However, implementations are free to expose tools through any interface pattern that
28	suits their needs—the protocol itself does not mandate any specific user
29	interaction model.
30	
31	<Warning>
32	
33	For trust & safety and security, there **SHOULD** always
34	be a human in the loop with the ability to deny tool invocations.
35	
36	Applications **SHOULD**:
37	
38	- Provide UI that makes clear which tools are being exposed to the AI model
39	- Insert clear visual indicators when tools are invoked
40	- Present confirmation prompts to the user for operations, to ensure a human is in the
41	  loop
42	
43	</Warning>
44	
45	## Capabilities
46	
47	Servers that support tools **MUST** declare the `tools` capability:
48	
49	```json
50	{
51	  "capabilities": {
52	    "tools": {
53	      "listChanged": true
54	    }
55	  }
56	}
57	```
58	
59	`listChanged` indicates whether the server will emit notifications when the list of
60	available tools changes.
61	
62	Servers that declare the `tools` capability **MUST** respond to `tools/list` requests
63	with the set of tools currently available to the requesting client. This set **MAY** be
64	empty and **MAY** change over time (see
65	[List Changed Notification](#list-changed-notification)), but **MUST NOT** vary
66	per-connection or as a side effect of other requests on the connection. The set
67	**MAY** vary by the authorization presented on the request — for example, returning
68	only the tools the caller's granted scopes permit — since credentials are
69	per-request input, not connection state.
70	
71	Servers **SHOULD** return tools in a deterministic order (i.e., the same ordering across
72	requests when the underlying set of tools has not changed). Deterministic ordering enables
73	clients to reliably cache the tool list and improves LLM prompt cache hit rates when tools
74	are included in model context.
75	
76	## Protocol Messages
77	
78	### Listing Tools
79	
80	To discover available tools, clients send a `tools/list` request. This operation supports
81	[pagination](/specification/2026-07-28/server/utilities/pagination) and [caching](/specification/2026-07-28/server/utilities/caching).
82	
83	**Request:**
84	
85	```json
86	{
87	  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
88	  "id": 1,
89	  "method": "tools/list",
90	  "params": {
91	    "cursor": "optional-cursor-value"
92	  }
93	}
94	```
95	
96	**Response:**
97	
98	```json
99	{
100	  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
101	  "id": 1,
102	  "result": {
103	    "resultType": "complete",
104	    "tools": [
105	      {
106	        "name": "get_weather",
107	        "title": "Weather Information Provider",
108	        "description": "Get current weather information for a location",
109	        "inputSchema": {
110	          "type": "object",
111	          "properties": {
112	            "location": {
113	              "type": "string",
114	              "description": "City name or zip code"
115	            }
116	          },
117	          "required": ["location"]
118	        },
119	        "icons": [
120	          {
121	            "src": "https://example.com/weather-icon.png",
122	            "mimeType": "image/png",
123	            "sizes": ["48x48"]
124	          }
125	        ]
126	      }
127	    ],
128	    "nextCursor": "next-page-cursor",
129	    "ttlMs": 300000,
130	    "cacheScope": "public"
131	  }
132	}
133	```
134	
135	### Calling Tools
136	
137	To invoke a tool, clients send a `tools/call` request:
138	
139	**Request:**
140	
141	```json
142	{
143	  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
144	  "id": 2,
145	  "method": "tools/call",
146	  "params": {
147	    "name": "get_weather",
148	    "arguments": {
149	      "location": "New York"
150	    }
151	  }
152	}
153	```
154	
155	**Response:**
156	
157	```json
158	{
159	  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
160	  "id": 2,
161	  "result": {
162	    "resultType": "complete",
163	    "content": [
164	      {
165	        "type": "text",
166	        "text": "Current weather in New York:\nTemperature: 72°F\nConditions: Partly cloudy"
167	      }
168	    ],
169	    "isError": false
170	  }
171	}
172	```
173	
174	### Input Required Tool Results
175	
176	Servers **MAY** respond to `tools/call` with an [`InputRequiredResult`](/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/mrtr#inputrequiredresult) to indicate that additional input is needed before the tool call can be completed. This follows the [multi round-trip requests](/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/mrtr#multi-round-trip-requests) mechanism.
177	
178	When retrying the request with input responses, clients include `inputResponses` and, if provided by the server, `requestState` in the request parameters:
179	
180	**Input Required Response:**
181	
182	```json
183	{
184	  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
185	  "id": 2,
186	  "result": {
187	    "resultType": "input_required",
188	    "inputRequests": {
189	      "github_login": {
190	        "method": "elicitation/create",
191	        "params": {
192	          "mode": "form",
193	          "message": "Please provide your GitHub username",
194	          "requestedSchema": {
195	            "type": "object",
196	            "properties": {
197	              "name": { "type": "string" }
198	            },
199	            "required": ["name"]
200	          }
201	        }
202	      }
203	    },
204	    "requestState": "eyJsb2NhdGlvbiI6Ik5ldyBZb3JrIn0..."
205	  }
206	}
207	```
208	
209	**Retry with Input Responses:**
210	
211	```json
212	{
213	  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
214	  "id": 3,
215	  "method": "tools/call",
216	  "params": {
217	    "name": "get_weather",
218	    "arguments": {
219	      "location": "New York"
220	    },
221	    "inputResponses": {
222	      "github_login": {
223	        "action": "accept",
224	        "content": {
225	          "name": "octocat"
226	        }
227	      }
228	    },
229	    "requestState": "eyJsb2NhdGlvbiI6Ik5ldyBZb3JrIn0..."
230	  }
231	}
232	```
233	
234	Note that the JSON-RPC `id` **MUST** be different between the initial request and the retry.
235	
236	### List Changed Notification
237	
238	When the list of available tools changes, servers that declared the `listChanged`
239	capability **SHOULD** send a notification to clients that have opened a
240	[`subscriptions/listen`](/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/subscriptions) stream with
241	`toolsListChanged: true`:
242	
243	```json
244	{
245	  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
246	  "method": "notifications/tools/list_changed"
247	}
248	```
249	
250	## Message Flow
251	
252	```mermaid
253	sequenceDiagram
254	    participant LLM
255	    participant Client
256	    participant Server
257	
258	    Note over Client,Server: Discovery
259	    Client->>Server: tools/list
260	    Server-->>Client: List of tools
261	
262	    Note over Client,LLM: Tool Selection
263	    LLM->>Client: Select tool to use
264	
265	    Note over Client,Server: Invocation
266	    Client->>Server: tools/call
267	    Server-->>Client: Tool result
268	    Client->>LLM: Process result
269	
270	    opt listChanged
271	      Client->>Server: subscriptions/listen (toolsListChanged: true)
272	      Server--)Client: notifications/subscriptions/acknowledged
273	      Note over Client,Server: Updates
274	      Server--)Client: notifications/tools/list_changed
275	      Client->>Server: tools/list
276	      Server-->>Client: Updated tools
277	    end
278	```
279	
280	## Data Types
281	
282	### Tool
283	
284	A tool definition includes:
285	
286	- `name`: Unique identifier for the tool
287	- `title`: Optional human-readable name of the tool for display purposes.
288	- `description`: Human-readable description of functionality
289	- `icons`: Optional array of icons for display in user interfaces
290	- `inputSchema`: JSON Schema defining expected parameters
291	  - Follows the [JSON Schema usage guidelines](/specification/2026-07-28/basic#json-schema-usage)
292	  - Defaults to 2020-12 if no `$schema` field is present
293	  - **MUST** be a valid JSON Schema object (not `null`)
294	  - For tools with no parameters, use one of these valid approaches:
295	    - `{ "type": "object", "additionalProperties": false }` - **Recommended**: explicitly accepts only empty objects
296	    - `{ "type": "object" }` - accepts any object (including with properties)
297	  - Properties **MAY** include an [`x-mcp-header`](#x-mcp-header) annotation to expose
298	    parameter values as HTTP headers
299	- `outputSchema`: Optional JSON Schema defining expected output structure
300	  - Follows the [JSON Schema usage guidelines](/specification/2026-07-28/basic#json-schema-usage)
301	  - Defaults to 2020-12 if no `$schema` field is present
302	- `annotations`: Optional properties describing tool behavior
303	
304	<Warning>
305	  For trust & safety and security, clients **MUST** consider tool annotations to
306	  be untrusted unless they come from trusted servers.
307	</Warning>
308	
309	#### Tool Names
310	
311	- Tool names **SHOULD** be between 1 and 128 characters in length (inclusive).
312	- Tool names **SHOULD** be considered case-sensitive.
313	- The following **SHOULD** be the only allowed characters: uppercase and lowercase ASCII letters (A-Z, a-z), digits
314	  (0-9), underscore (\_), hyphen (-), and dot (.)
315	- Tool names **SHOULD NOT** contain spaces, commas, or other special characters.
316	- Tool names **SHOULD** be unique within a server.
317	- Example valid tool names:
318	  - `getUser`
319	  - `DATA_EXPORT_v2`
320	  - `admin.tools.list`
321	
322	<Note>
323	
324	Tool name uniqueness is scoped to a single server. Clients or proxies that
325	aggregate tools from multiple servers **MAY** encounter naming collisions (for
326	example, two servers each exposing a `search` tool) and **SHOULD** implement a
327	disambiguation strategy such as prefixing tool names with a server identifier.
328	
329	The server `name` (from `serverInfo`) is not guaranteed to be unique across
330	servers and **SHOULD NOT** be relied upon for disambiguation.
331	
332	</Note>
333	
334	#### x-mcp-header
335	
336	The `x-mcp-header` extension property allows servers to designate specific tool
337	parameters to be mirrored into HTTP headers when using the
338	[Streamable HTTP transport](/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/streamable-http#custom-headers-from-tool-parameters).
339	This enables network intermediaries (load balancers, proxies, WAFs) to route and process
340	requests based on parameter values without parsing the request body.
341	
342	The `x-mcp-header` property is placed directly within the JSON Schema of the property to
343	be mirrored. Its value specifies the name portion of the resulting `Mcp-Param-{name}`
344	HTTP header.
345	
346	**Constraints on `x-mcp-header` values:**
347	
348	- **MUST NOT** be empty
349	- **MUST** match HTTP field-name token syntax (`1*tchar`, [RFC 9110 Section 5.1](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9110#section-5.1))
350	- **MUST NOT** contain control characters, including carriage return (CR, `\r`) or
351	  line feed (LF, `\n`)
352	- **MUST** be case-insensitively unique among all `x-mcp-header` values in the
353	  `inputSchema`
354	- **MUST** only be applied to parameters with primitive types (integer, string, boolean).
355	  Parameters with type `number` are not permitted. Integer values **MUST** be within the
356	  safe range for integers represented using IEEE754 double-precision floating point numbers (−2<sup>53</sup>+1 to 2<sup>53</sup>−1)
357	- **MUST** only be applied to properties that are _statically reachable_ from the schema
358	  root, as defined in
359	  [Custom Headers from Tool Parameters](/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/streamable-http#custom-headers-from-tool-parameters),
360	  which also defines how header values are extracted from call arguments
361	
362	Clients using the Streamable HTTP transport **MUST** reject tool definitions where any
363	`x-mcp-header` value violates these constraints. Rejection means the client **MUST**
364	exclude the invalid tool from the result of `tools/list`. Clients **SHOULD** log a
365	warning when rejecting a tool definition, including the tool name and the reason for
366	rejection. This ensures that a single malformed tool definition does not prevent other
367	valid tools from being used. Clients using other transports (e.g., stdio) **MAY** ignore
368	`x-mcp-header` annotations entirely.
369	
370	**Example tool definition with `x-mcp-header`:**
371	
372	```json
373	{
374	  "name": "execute_sql",
375	  "description": "Execute SQL on Google Cloud Spanner",
376	  "inputSchema": {
377	    "type": "object",
378	    "properties": {
379	      "region": {
380	        "type": "string",
381	        "description": "The region to execute the query in",
382	        "x-mcp-header": "Region"
383	      },
384	      "query": {
385	        "type": "string",
386	        "description": "The SQL query to execute"
387	      }
388	    },
389	    "required": ["region", "query"]
390	  }
391	}
392	```
393	
394	In this example, when the tool is called with `"region": "us-west1"`, the client adds
395	the header `Mcp-Param-Region: us-west1` to the HTTP request.
396	
397	<Warning>
398	
399	Server developers **SHOULD NOT** mark sensitive parameters (passwords, API keys, tokens,
400	PII) with `x-mcp-header`, as header values are visible to network intermediaries.
401	
402	</Warning>
403	
404	### Tool Result
405	
406	Tool results may contain [**structured**](#structured-content) or **unstructured** content.
407	
408	**Unstructured** content is returned in the `content` field of a result, and can contain multiple content items of different types:
409	
410	<Note>
411	  All content types (text, image, audio, resource links, and embedded resources)
412	  support optional
413	  [annotations](/specification/2026-07-28/server/resources#annotations) that
414	  provide metadata about audience, priority, and modification times. This is the
415	  same annotation format used by resources and prompts.
416	</Note>
417	
418	#### Text Content
419	
420	```json
421	{
422	  "type": "text",
423	  "text": "Tool result text"
424	}
425	```
426	
427	#### Image Content
428	
429	```json
430	{
431	  "type": "image",
432	  "data": "base64-encoded-data",
433	  "mimeType": "image/png",
434	  "annotations": {
435	    "audience": ["user"],
436	    "priority": 0.9
437	  }
438	}
439	```
440	
441	#### Audio Content
442	
443	```json
444	{
445	  "type": "audio",
446	  "data": "base64-encoded-audio-data",
447	  "mimeType": "audio/wav"
448	}
449	```
450	
451	#### Resource Links
452	
453	A tool **MAY** return links to [Resources](/specification/2026-07-28/server/resources), to provide additional context
454	or data. In this case, the tool will return a URI that can be subscribed to or fetched by the client:
455	
456	```json
457	{
458	  "type": "resource_link",
459	  "uri": "file:///project/src/main.rs",
460	  "name": "main.rs",
461	  "description": "Primary application entry point",
462	  "mimeType": "text/x-rust"
463	}
464	```
465	
466	Resource links support the same [Resource annotations](/specification/2026-07-28/server/resources#annotations) as regular resources to help clients understand how to use them.
467	
468	<Info>
469	  Resource links returned by tools are not guaranteed to appear in the results
470	  of a `resources/list` request.
471	</Info>
472	
473	#### Embedded Resources
474	
475	[Resources](/specification/2026-07-28/server/resources) **MAY** be embedded to provide additional context
476	or data using a suitable [URI scheme](./resources#common-uri-schemes). Servers that use embedded resources **SHOULD** implement the `resources` capability:
477	
478	```json
479	{
480	  "type": "resource",
481	  "resource": {
482	    "uri": "file:///project/src/main.rs",
483	    "mimeType": "text/x-rust",
484	    "text": "fn main() {\n    println!(\"Hello world!\");\n}",
485	    "annotations": {
486	      "audience": ["user", "assistant"],
487	      "priority": 0.7,
488	      "lastModified": "2025-05-03T14:30:00Z"
489	    }
490	  }
491	}
492	```
493	
494	Embedded resources support the same [Resource annotations](/specification/2026-07-28/server/resources#annotations) as regular resources to help clients understand how to use them.
495	
496	#### Structured Content
497	
498	**Structured** content is returned as a JSON value in the `structuredContent` field of a result. This can be any JSON value (object, array, string, number, boolean, or null) that conforms to the tool's `outputSchema` if one is defined.
499	
500	For backwards compatibility, a tool that returns structured content SHOULD also return the serialized JSON in a TextContent block.
501	
502	<Note>
503	
504	`structuredContent` is server-produced result data and is unrelated to LLM
505	"structured outputs" (schema-constrained model generation).
506	
507	</Note>
508	
509	#### Output Schema
510	
511	Tools may also provide an output schema for validation of structured results.
512	If an output schema is provided:
513	
514	- Servers **MUST** provide structured results that conform to this schema.
515	- Clients **SHOULD** validate structured results against this schema.
516	
517	Example tool with output schema:
518	
519	```json
520	{
521	  "name": "get_weather_data",
522	  "title": "Weather Data Retriever",
523	  "description": "Get current weather data for a location",
524	  "inputSchema": {
525	    "type": "object",
526	    "properties": {
527	      "location": {
528	        "type": "string",
529	        "description": "City name or zip code"
530	      }
531	    },
532	    "required": ["location"]
533	  },
534	  "outputSchema": {
535	    "type": "object",
536	    "properties": {
537	      "temperature": {
538	        "type": "number",
539	        "description": "Temperature in celsius"
540	      },
541	      "conditions": {
542	        "type": "string",
543	        "description": "Weather conditions description"
544	      },
545	      "humidity": {
546	        "type": "number",
547	        "description": "Humidity percentage"
548	      }
549	    },
550	    "required": ["temperature", "conditions", "humidity"]
551	  }
552	}
553	```
554	
555	Example valid response for this tool:
556	
557	```json
558	{
559	  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
560	  "id": 5,
561	  "result": {
562	    "resultType": "complete",
563	    "content": [
564	      {
565	        "type": "text",
566	        "text": "{\"temperature\": 22.5, \"conditions\": \"Partly cloudy\", \"humidity\": 65}"
567	      }
568	    ],
569	    "structuredContent": {
570	      "temperature": 22.5,
571	      "conditions": "Partly cloudy",
572	      "humidity": 65
573	    }
574	  }
575	}
576	```
577	
578	Example tool with array output schema:
579	
580	```json
581	{
582	  "name": "list_users",
583	  "title": "User List",
584	  "description": "Returns a list of all users",
585	  "inputSchema": {
586	    "type": "object",
587	    "properties": {}
588	  },
589	  "outputSchema": {
590	    "type": "array",
591	    "items": {
592	      "type": "object",
593	      "properties": {
594	        "id": { "type": "string" },
595	        "name": { "type": "string" },
596	        "email": { "type": "string" }
597	      },
598	      "required": ["id", "name", "email"]
599	    }
600	  }
601	}
602	```
603	
604	Example valid response for a tool with array output:
605	
606	```json
607	{
608	  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
609	  "id": 6,
610	  "result": {
611	    "resultType": "complete",
612	    "content": [
613	      {
614	        "type": "text",
615	        "text": "Found 2 users: Alice (alice@example.com) and Bob (bob@example.com)."
616	      }
617	    ],
618	    "structuredContent": [
619	      { "id": "1", "name": "Alice", "email": "alice@example.com" },
620	      { "id": "2", "name": "Bob", "email": "bob@example.com" }
621	    ]
622	  }
623	}
624	```
625	
626	Providing an output schema helps clients and LLMs understand and properly handle structured tool outputs by:
627	
628	- Enabling strict schema validation of responses
629	- Providing type information for better integration with programming languages
630	- Guiding clients and LLMs to properly parse and utilize the returned data
631	- Supporting better documentation and developer experience
632	
633	### Schema Examples
634	
635	#### Tool with default 2020-12 schema:
636	
637	```json
638	{
639	  "name": "calculate_sum",
640	  "description": "Add two numbers",
641	  "inputSchema": {
642	    "type": "object",
643	    "properties": {
644	      "a": { "type": "number" },
645	      "b": { "type": "number" }
646	    },
647	    "required": ["a", "b"]
648	  }
649	}
650	```
651	
652	#### Tool with explicit draft-07 schema:
653	
654	```json
655	{
656	  "name": "calculate_sum",
657	  "description": "Add two numbers",
658	  "inputSchema": {
659	    "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#",
660	    "type": "object",
661	    "properties": {
662	      "a": { "type": "number" },
663	      "b": { "type": "number" }
664	    },
665	    "required": ["a", "b"]
666	  }
667	}
668	```
669	
670	#### Tool with no parameters:
671	
672	```json
673	{
674	  "name": "get_current_time",
675	  "description": "Returns the current server time",
676	  "inputSchema": {
677	    "type": "object",
678	    "additionalProperties": false
679	  }
680	}
681	```
682	
683	## Stateful Tools
684	
685	<Note>
686	
687	This section is non-normative guidance for tool design. The protocol has no
688	concept of a state handle; from the wire's perspective a handle is an ordinary
689	string in a tool result and an ordinary argument to subsequent tool calls.
690	
691	</Note>
692	
693	MCP has no protocol-level session, so a server cannot rely on implicit
694	per-connection state to relate one tool call to the next. Servers that need to
695	maintain state across calls — a shopping cart, an open browser context, a
696	database transaction — should do so by returning an explicit handle from a
697	creation tool and accepting that handle as an argument on subsequent calls.
698	
699	For example, a server that manages a shopping cart might expose:
700	
701	```jsonc
702	// → tools/call
703	{ "name": "create_basket", "arguments": {} }
704	
705	// ← result
706	{
707	  "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "Created basket bsk_a1b2c3" }],
708	  "structuredContent": { "basket_id": "bsk_a1b2c3" }
709	}
710	
711	// → tools/call
712	{
713	  "name": "add_item",
714	  "arguments": { "basket_id": "bsk_a1b2c3", "sku": "..." }
715	}
716	```
717	
718	The model is responsible for carrying `basket_id` forward; the server stores
719	the cart contents under that key and looks them up on each call.
720	
721	When designing handles, servers should consider:
722	
723	- **Authorization.** For authenticated servers, a handle is a name, not a
724	  capability. The server should validate the caller's authorization against the
725	  handle on every call. For unauthenticated servers, where the handle is
726	  necessarily a bearer token, it should be generated with sufficient entropy
727	  (e.g., a UUIDv4) and given a bounded lifetime.
728	- **Opacity.** Handles that encode internal structure invite parsing or
729	  guessing; opaque identifiers do not.
730	- **Lifetime.** Because handles outlive any single connection, the server's
731	  retention policy should be stated in the creation tool's description (e.g.,
732	  "baskets expire after 24 hours of inactivity") so the model can see it when
733	  deciding to create state.
734	- **Expiry errors.** A call against an expired or unknown handle should return
735	  a tool execution error that says so, so the model can recover by creating a
736	  new one.
737	
738	## Error Handling
739	
740	Tools use two error reporting mechanisms:
741	
742	1. **Protocol Errors** indicate issues with the request structure itself that models are less likely to be able to fix:
743	   - Unknown tool
744	   - Malformed requests (requests that fail to satisfy [CallToolRequest schema](/specification/2026-07-28/schema#calltoolrequest))
745	   - Server errors
746	
747	   They are returned as standard JSON-RPC errors:
748	
749	   ```json
750	   {
751	     "jsonrpc": "2.0",
752	     "id": 3,
753	     "error": {
754	       "code": -32602,
755	       "message": "Unknown tool: invalid_tool_name"
756	     }
757	   }
758	   ```
759	
760	2. **Tool Execution Errors** contain actionable feedback that language models can use to self-correct and retry with adjusted parameters:
761	   - API failures
762	   - Input validation errors (e.g., date in wrong format, value out of range)
763	   - Business logic errors
764	
765	   They are reported in tool results with `isError: true`:
766	
767	   ```json
768	   {
769	     "jsonrpc": "2.0",
770	     "id": 4,
771	     "result": {
772	       "resultType": "complete",
773	       "content": [
774	         {
775	           "type": "text",
776	           "text": "Invalid departure date: must be in the future. Current date is 08/08/2025."
777	         }
778	       ],
779	       "isError": true
780	     }
781	   }
782	   ```
783	
784	Clients **MAY** provide protocol errors to language models, though these are less likely to result in successful recovery.
785	Clients **SHOULD** provide tool execution errors to language models to enable self-correction.
786	
787	## Security Considerations
788	
789	1. Servers **MUST**:
790	   - Validate all tool inputs
791	   - Implement proper access controls
792	   - Rate limit tool invocations
793	   - Sanitize tool outputs
794	
795	2. Clients **SHOULD**:
796	   - Prompt for user confirmation on sensitive operations
797	   - Show tool inputs to the user before calling the server, to avoid malicious or
798	     accidental data exfiltration
799	   - Validate tool results before passing to LLM
800	   - Follow the [`$ref` resolution requirements](/specification/2026-07-28/basic/index#ref-resolution)
801	     when validating tool inputs and outputs against `inputSchema` and `outputSchema`
802	   - Implement timeouts for tool calls
803	   - Log tool usage for audit purposes
804

---
title: Tools
---

<div id="enable-section-numbers" />

The Model Context Protocol (MCP) allows servers to expose tools that can be invoked by
language models. Tools enable models to interact with external systems, such as querying
databases, calling APIs, or performing computations. Each tool is uniquely identified by
a name and includes metadata describing its schema.

<Note>
  For brevity, the request examples on this page omit the `_meta` request
  metadata (`io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion`,
  `io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo`, and
  `io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities`). Every request **MUST** include
  the required `_meta` fields; see
  [`_meta`](/specification/2026-07-28/basic/index#meta).
</Note>

## User Interaction Model

Tools in MCP are designed to be **model-controlled**, meaning that the language model can
discover and invoke tools automatically based on its contextual understanding and the
user's prompts.

However, implementations are free to expose tools through any interface pattern that
suits their needs—the protocol itself does not mandate any specific user
interaction model.

<Warning>

For trust & safety and security, there **SHOULD** always
be a human in the loop with the ability to deny tool invocations.

Applications **SHOULD**:

- Provide UI that makes clear which tools are being exposed to the AI model
- Insert clear visual indicators when tools are invoked
- Present confirmation prompts to the user for operations, to ensure a human is in the
  loop

</Warning>

## Capabilities

Servers that support tools **MUST** declare the `tools` capability:

```json
{
  "capabilities": {
    "tools": {
      "listChanged": true
    }
  }
}
```

`listChanged` indicates whether the server will emit notifications when the list of
available tools changes.

Servers that declare the `tools` capability **MUST** respond to `tools/list` requests
with the set of tools currently available to the requesting client. This set **MAY** be
empty and **MAY** change over time (see
[List Changed Notification](#list-changed-notification)), but **MUST NOT** vary
per-connection or as a side effect of other requests on the connection. The set
**MAY** vary by the authorization presented on the request — for example, returning
only the tools the caller's granted scopes permit — since credentials are
per-request input, not connection state.

Servers **SHOULD** return tools in a deterministic order (i.e., the same ordering across
requests when the underlying set of tools has not changed). Deterministic ordering enables
clients to reliably cache the tool list and improves LLM prompt cache hit rates when tools
are included in model context.

## Protocol Messages

### Listing Tools

To discover available tools, clients send a `tools/list` request. This operation supports
[pagination](/specification/2026-07-28/server/utilities/pagination) and [caching](/specification/2026-07-28/server/utilities/caching).

**Request:**

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "method": "tools/list",
  "params": {
    "cursor": "optional-cursor-value"
  }
}
```

**Response:**

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "result": {
    "resultType": "complete",
    "tools": [
      {
        "name": "get_weather",
        "title": "Weather Information Provider",
        "description": "Get current weather information for a location",
        "inputSchema": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {
            "location": {
              "type": "string",
              "description": "City name or zip code"
            }
          },
          "required": ["location"]
        },
        "icons": [
          {
            "src": "https://example.com/weather-icon.png",
            "mimeType": "image/png",
            "sizes": ["48x48"]
          }
        ]
      }
    ],
    "nextCursor": "next-page-cursor",
    "ttlMs": 300000,
    "cacheScope": "public"
  }
}
```

### Calling Tools

To invoke a tool, clients send a `tools/call` request:

**Request:**

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 2,
  "method": "tools/call",
  "params": {
    "name": "get_weather",
    "arguments": {
      "location": "New York"
    }
  }
}
```

**Response:**

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 2,
  "result": {
    "resultType": "complete",
    "content": [
      {
        "type": "text",
        "text": "Current weather in New York:\nTemperature: 72°F\nConditions: Partly cloudy"
      }
    ],
    "isError": false
  }
}
```

### Input Required Tool Results

Servers **MAY** respond to `tools/call` with an [`InputRequiredResult`](/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/mrtr#inputrequiredresult) to indicate that additional input is needed before the tool call can be completed. This follows the [multi round-trip requests](/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/mrtr#multi-round-trip-requests) mechanism.

When retrying the request with input responses, clients include `inputResponses` and, if provided by the server, `requestState` in the request parameters:

**Input Required Response:**

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 2,
  "result": {
    "resultType": "input_required",
    "inputRequests": {
      "github_login": {
        "method": "elicitation/create",
        "params": {
          "mode": "form",
          "message": "Please provide your GitHub username",
          "requestedSchema": {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {
              "name": { "type": "string" }
            },
            "required": ["name"]
          }
        }
      }
    },
    "requestState": "eyJsb2NhdGlvbiI6Ik5ldyBZb3JrIn0..."
  }
}
```

**Retry with Input Responses:**

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 3,
  "method": "tools/call",
  "params": {
    "name": "get_weather",
    "arguments": {
      "location": "New York"
    },
    "inputResponses": {
      "github_login": {
        "action": "accept",
        "content": {
          "name": "octocat"
        }
      }
    },
    "requestState": "eyJsb2NhdGlvbiI6Ik5ldyBZb3JrIn0..."
  }
}
```

Note that the JSON-RPC `id` **MUST** be different between the initial request and the retry.

### List Changed Notification

When the list of available tools changes, servers that declared the `listChanged`
capability **SHOULD** send a notification to clients that have opened a
[`subscriptions/listen`](/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/subscriptions) stream with
`toolsListChanged: true`:

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "method": "notifications/tools/list_changed"
}
```

## Message Flow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant LLM
    participant Client
    participant Server

    Note over Client,Server: Discovery
    Client->>Server: tools/list
    Server-->>Client: List of tools

    Note over Client,LLM: Tool Selection
    LLM->>Client: Select tool to use

    Note over Client,Server: Invocation
    Client->>Server: tools/call
    Server-->>Client: Tool result
    Client->>LLM: Process result

    opt listChanged
      Client->>Server: subscriptions/listen (toolsListChanged: true)
      Server--)Client: notifications/subscriptions/acknowledged
      Note over Client,Server: Updates
      Server--)Client: notifications/tools/list_changed
      Client->>Server: tools/list
      Server-->>Client: Updated tools
    end
```

## Data Types

### Tool

A tool definition includes:

- `name`: Unique identifier for the tool
- `title`: Optional human-readable name of the tool for display purposes.
- `description`: Human-readable description of functionality
- `icons`: Optional array of icons for display in user interfaces
- `inputSchema`: JSON Schema defining expected parameters
  - Follows the [JSON Schema usage guidelines](/specification/2026-07-28/basic#json-schema-usage)
  - Defaults to 2020-12 if no `$schema` field is present
  - **MUST** be a valid JSON Schema object (not `null`)
  - For tools with no parameters, use one of these valid approaches:
    - `{ "type": "object", "additionalProperties": false }` - **Recommended**: explicitly accepts only empty objects
    - `{ "type": "object" }` - accepts any object (including with properties)
  - Properties **MAY** include an [`x-mcp-header`](#x-mcp-header) annotation to expose
    parameter values as HTTP headers
- `outputSchema`: Optional JSON Schema defining expected output structure
  - Follows the [JSON Schema usage guidelines](/specification/2026-07-28/basic#json-schema-usage)
  - Defaults to 2020-12 if no `$schema` field is present
- `annotations`: Optional properties describing tool behavior

<Warning>
  For trust & safety and security, clients **MUST** consider tool annotations to
  be untrusted unless they come from trusted servers.
</Warning>

#### Tool Names

- Tool names **SHOULD** be between 1 and 128 characters in length (inclusive).
- Tool names **SHOULD** be considered case-sensitive.
- The following **SHOULD** be the only allowed characters: uppercase and lowercase ASCII letters (A-Z, a-z), digits
  (0-9), underscore (\_), hyphen (-), and dot (.)
- Tool names **SHOULD NOT** contain spaces, commas, or other special characters.
- Tool names **SHOULD** be unique within a server.
- Example valid tool names:
  - `getUser`
  - `DATA_EXPORT_v2`
  - `admin.tools.list`

<Note>

Tool name uniqueness is scoped to a single server. Clients or proxies that
aggregate tools from multiple servers **MAY** encounter naming collisions (for
example, two servers each exposing a `search` tool) and **SHOULD** implement a
disambiguation strategy such as prefixing tool names with a server identifier.

The server `name` (from `serverInfo`) is not guaranteed to be unique across
servers and **SHOULD NOT** be relied upon for disambiguation.

</Note>

#### x-mcp-header

The `x-mcp-header` extension property allows servers to designate specific tool
parameters to be mirrored into HTTP headers when using the
[Streamable HTTP transport](/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/streamable-http#custom-headers-from-tool-parameters).
This enables network intermediaries (load balancers, proxies, WAFs) to route and process
requests based on parameter values without parsing the request body.

The `x-mcp-header` property is placed directly within the JSON Schema of the property to
be mirrored. Its value specifies the name portion of the resulting `Mcp-Param-{name}`
HTTP header.

**Constraints on `x-mcp-header` values:**

- **MUST NOT** be empty
- **MUST** match HTTP field-name token syntax (`1*tchar`, [RFC 9110 Section 5.1](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9110#section-5.1))
- **MUST NOT** contain control characters, including carriage return (CR, `\r`) or
  line feed (LF, `\n`)
- **MUST** be case-insensitively unique among all `x-mcp-header` values in the
  `inputSchema`
- **MUST** only be applied to parameters with primitive types (integer, string, boolean).
  Parameters with type `number` are not permitted. Integer values **MUST** be within the
  safe range for integers represented using IEEE754 double-precision floating point numbers (−2<sup>53</sup>+1 to 2<sup>53</sup>−1)
- **MUST** only be applied to properties that are _statically reachable_ from the schema
  root, as defined in
  [Custom Headers from Tool Parameters](/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/streamable-http#custom-headers-from-tool-parameters),
  which also defines how header values are extracted from call arguments

Clients using the Streamable HTTP transport **MUST** reject tool definitions where any
`x-mcp-header` value violates these constraints. Rejection means the client **MUST**
exclude the invalid tool from the result of `tools/list`. Clients **SHOULD** log a
warning when rejecting a tool definition, including the tool name and the reason for
rejection. This ensures that a single malformed tool definition does not prevent other
valid tools from being used. Clients using other transports (e.g., stdio) **MAY** ignore
`x-mcp-header` annotations entirely.

**Example tool definition with `x-mcp-header`:**

```json
{
  "name": "execute_sql",
  "description": "Execute SQL on Google Cloud Spanner",
  "inputSchema": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
      "region": {
        "type": "string",
        "description": "The region to execute the query in",
        "x-mcp-header": "Region"
      },
      "query": {
        "type": "string",
        "description": "The SQL query to execute"
      }
    },
    "required": ["region", "query"]
  }
}
```

In this example, when the tool is called with `"region": "us-west1"`, the client adds
the header `Mcp-Param-Region: us-west1` to the HTTP request.

<Warning>

Server developers **SHOULD NOT** mark sensitive parameters (passwords, API keys, tokens,
PII) with `x-mcp-header`, as header values are visible to network intermediaries.

</Warning>

### Tool Result

Tool results may contain [**structured**](#structured-content) or **unstructured** content.

**Unstructured** content is returned in the `content` field of a result, and can contain multiple content items of different types:

<Note>
  All content types (text, image, audio, resource links, and embedded resources)
  support optional
  [annotations](/specification/2026-07-28/server/resources#annotations) that
  provide metadata about audience, priority, and modification times. This is the
  same annotation format used by resources and prompts.
</Note>

#### Text Content

```json
{
  "type": "text",
  "text": "Tool result text"
}
```

#### Image Content

```json
{
  "type": "image",
  "data": "base64-encoded-data",
  "mimeType": "image/png",
  "annotations": {
    "audience": ["user"],
    "priority": 0.9
  }
}
```

#### Audio Content

```json
{
  "type": "audio",
  "data": "base64-encoded-audio-data",
  "mimeType": "audio/wav"
}
```

#### Resource Links

A tool **MAY** return links to [Resources](/specification/2026-07-28/server/resources), to provide additional context
or data. In this case, the tool will return a URI that can be subscribed to or fetched by the client:

```json
{
  "type": "resource_link",
  "uri": "file:///project/src/main.rs",
  "name": "main.rs",
  "description": "Primary application entry point",
  "mimeType": "text/x-rust"
}
```

Resource links support the same [Resource annotations](/specification/2026-07-28/server/resources#annotations) as regular resources to help clients understand how to use them.

<Info>
  Resource links returned by tools are not guaranteed to appear in the results
  of a `resources/list` request.
</Info>

#### Embedded Resources

[Resources](/specification/2026-07-28/server/resources) **MAY** be embedded to provide additional context
or data using a suitable [URI scheme](./resources#common-uri-schemes). Servers that use embedded resources **SHOULD** implement the `resources` capability:

```json
{
  "type": "resource",
  "resource": {
    "uri": "file:///project/src/main.rs",
    "mimeType": "text/x-rust",
    "text": "fn main() {\n    println!(\"Hello world!\");\n}",
    "annotations": {
      "audience": ["user", "assistant"],
      "priority": 0.7,
      "lastModified": "2025-05-03T14:30:00Z"
    }
  }
}
```

Embedded resources support the same [Resource annotations](/specification/2026-07-28/server/resources#annotations) as regular resources to help clients understand how to use them.

#### Structured Content

**Structured** content is returned as a JSON value in the `structuredContent` field of a result. This can be any JSON value (object, array, string, number, boolean, or null) that conforms to the tool's `outputSchema` if one is defined.

For backwards compatibility, a tool that returns structured content SHOULD also return the serialized JSON in a TextContent block.

<Note>

`structuredContent` is server-produced result data and is unrelated to LLM
"structured outputs" (schema-constrained model generation).

</Note>

#### Output Schema

Tools may also provide an output schema for validation of structured results.
If an output schema is provided:

- Servers **MUST** provide structured results that conform to this schema.
- Clients **SHOULD** validate structured results against this schema.

Example tool with output schema:

```json
{
  "name": "get_weather_data",
  "title": "Weather Data Retriever",
  "description": "Get current weather data for a location",
  "inputSchema": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
      "location": {
        "type": "string",
        "description": "City name or zip code"
      }
    },
    "required": ["location"]
  },
  "outputSchema": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
      "temperature": {
        "type": "number",
        "description": "Temperature in celsius"
      },
      "conditions": {
        "type": "string",
        "description": "Weather conditions description"
      },
      "humidity": {
        "type": "number",
        "description": "Humidity percentage"
      }
    },
    "required": ["temperature", "conditions", "humidity"]
  }
}
```

Example valid response for this tool:

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 5,
  "result": {
    "resultType": "complete",
    "content": [
      {
        "type": "text",
        "text": "{\"temperature\": 22.5, \"conditions\": \"Partly cloudy\", \"humidity\": 65}"
      }
    ],
    "structuredContent": {
      "temperature": 22.5,
      "conditions": "Partly cloudy",
      "humidity": 65
    }
  }
}
```

Example tool with array output schema:

```json
{
  "name": "list_users",
  "title": "User List",
  "description": "Returns a list of all users",
  "inputSchema": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {}
  },
  "outputSchema": {
    "type": "array",
    "items": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "id": { "type": "string" },
        "name": { "type": "string" },
        "email": { "type": "string" }
      },
      "required": ["id", "name", "email"]
    }
  }
}
```

Example valid response for a tool with array output:

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 6,
  "result": {
    "resultType": "complete",
    "content": [
      {
        "type": "text",
        "text": "Found 2 users: Alice (alice@example.com) and Bob (bob@example.com)."
      }
    ],
    "structuredContent": [
      { "id": "1", "name": "Alice", "email": "alice@example.com" },
      { "id": "2", "name": "Bob", "email": "bob@example.com" }
    ]
  }
}
```

Providing an output schema helps clients and LLMs understand and properly handle structured tool outputs by:

- Enabling strict schema validation of responses
- Providing type information for better integration with programming languages
- Guiding clients and LLMs to properly parse and utilize the returned data
- Supporting better documentation and developer experience

### Schema Examples

#### Tool with default 2020-12 schema:

```json
{
  "name": "calculate_sum",
  "description": "Add two numbers",
  "inputSchema": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
      "a": { "type": "number" },
      "b": { "type": "number" }
    },
    "required": ["a", "b"]
  }
}
```

#### Tool with explicit draft-07 schema:

```json
{
  "name": "calculate_sum",
  "description": "Add two numbers",
  "inputSchema": {
    "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#",
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
      "a": { "type": "number" },
      "b": { "type": "number" }
    },
    "required": ["a", "b"]
  }
}
```

#### Tool with no parameters:

```json
{
  "name": "get_current_time",
  "description": "Returns the current server time",
  "inputSchema": {
    "type": "object",
    "additionalProperties": false
  }
}
```

## Stateful Tools

<Note>

This section is non-normative guidance for tool design. The protocol has no
concept of a state handle; from the wire's perspective a handle is an ordinary
string in a tool result and an ordinary argument to subsequent tool calls.

</Note>

MCP has no protocol-level session, so a server cannot rely on implicit
per-connection state to relate one tool call to the next. Servers that need to
maintain state across calls — a shopping cart, an open browser context, a
database transaction — should do so by returning an explicit handle from a
creation tool and accepting that handle as an argument on subsequent calls.

For example, a server that manages a shopping cart might expose:

```jsonc
// → tools/call
{ "name": "create_basket", "arguments": {} }

// ← result
{
  "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "Created basket bsk_a1b2c3" }],
  "structuredContent": { "basket_id": "bsk_a1b2c3" }
}

// → tools/call
{
  "name": "add_item",
  "arguments": { "basket_id": "bsk_a1b2c3", "sku": "..." }
}
```

The model is responsible for carrying `basket_id` forward; the server stores
the cart contents under that key and looks them up on each call.

When designing handles, servers should consider:

- **Authorization.** For authenticated servers, a handle is a name, not a
  capability. The server should validate the caller's authorization against the
  handle on every call. For unauthenticated servers, where the handle is
  necessarily a bearer token, it should be generated with sufficient entropy
  (e.g., a UUIDv4) and given a bounded lifetime.
- **Opacity.** Handles that encode internal structure invite parsing or
  guessing; opaque identifiers do not.
- **Lifetime.** Because handles outlive any single connection, the server's
  retention policy should be stated in the creation tool's description (e.g.,
  "baskets expire after 24 hours of inactivity") so the model can see it when
  deciding to create state.
- **Expiry errors.** A call against an expired or unknown handle should return
  a tool execution error that says so, so the model can recover by creating a
  new one.

## Error Handling

Tools use two error reporting mechanisms:

1. **Protocol Errors** indicate issues with the request structure itself that models are less likely to be able to fix:
   - Unknown tool
   - Malformed requests (requests that fail to satisfy [CallToolRequest schema](/specification/2026-07-28/schema#calltoolrequest))
   - Server errors

   They are returned as standard JSON-RPC errors:

   ```json
   {
     "jsonrpc": "2.0",
     "id": 3,
     "error": {
       "code": -32602,
       "message": "Unknown tool: invalid_tool_name"
     }
   }
   ```

2. **Tool Execution Errors** contain actionable feedback that language models can use to self-correct and retry with adjusted parameters:
   - API failures
   - Input validation errors (e.g., date in wrong format, value out of range)
   - Business logic errors

   They are reported in tool results with `isError: true`:

   ```json
   {
     "jsonrpc": "2.0",
     "id": 4,
     "result": {
       "resultType": "complete",
       "content": [
         {
           "type": "text",
           "text": "Invalid departure date: must be in the future. Current date is 08/08/2025."
         }
       ],
       "isError": true
     }
   }
   ```

Clients **MAY** provide protocol errors to language models, though these are less likely to result in successful recovery.
Clients **SHOULD** provide tool execution errors to language models to enable self-correction.

## Security Considerations

1. Servers **MUST**:
   - Validate all tool inputs
   - Implement proper access controls
   - Rate limit tool invocations
   - Sanitize tool outputs

2. Clients **SHOULD**:
   - Prompt for user confirmation on sensitive operations
   - Show tool inputs to the user before calling the server, to avoid malicious or
     accidental data exfiltration
   - Validate tool results before passing to LLM
   - Follow the [`$ref` resolution requirements](/specification/2026-07-28/basic/index#ref-resolution)
     when validating tool inputs and outputs against `inputSchema` and `outputSchema`
   - Implement timeouts for tool calls
   - Log tool usage for audit purposes

2	title: Resources

4	
5	<div id="enable-section-numbers" />
6	
7	The Model Context Protocol (MCP) provides a standardized way for servers to expose
8	resources to clients. Resources allow servers to share data that provides context to
9	language models, such as files, database schemas, or application-specific information.
10	Each resource is uniquely identified by a
11	[URI](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3986).
12	
13	<Note>
14	  For brevity, the request examples on this page omit the `_meta` request
15	  metadata (`io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion`,
16	  `io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo`, and
17	  `io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities`). Every request **MUST** include
18	  the required `_meta` fields; see
19	  [`_meta`](/specification/2026-07-28/basic/index#meta).
20	</Note>
21	
22	## User Interaction Model
23	
24	Resources in MCP are designed to be **application-driven**, with host applications
25	determining how to incorporate context based on their needs.
26	
27	For example, applications could:
28	
29	- Expose resources through UI elements for explicit selection, in a tree or list view
30	- Allow the user to search through and filter available resources
31	- Implement automatic context inclusion, based on heuristics or the AI model's selection
32	
33	![Example of resource context picker](/specification/2026-07-28/server/resource-picker.png)
34	
35	However, implementations are free to expose resources through any interface pattern that
36	suits their needs—the protocol itself does not mandate any specific user
37	interaction model.
38	
39	## Capabilities
40	
41	Servers that support resources **MUST** declare the `resources` capability:
42	
43	```json
44	{
45	  "capabilities": {
46	    "resources": {
47	      "listChanged": true,
48	      "subscribe": true
49	    }
50	  }
51	}
52	```
53	
54	The capability supports two optional features:
55	
56	- `listChanged`: whether the server will emit notifications when the list of available
57	  resources changes.
58	- `subscribe` : whether the server supports resource-specific update notifications
59	  for resources requested through subscriptions/listen using the resourceSubscriptions
60	  filter.
61	
62	Servers may advertise either feature independently, together or neither.
63	
64	Servers that support neither `listChanged` nor `subscribe` may omit it:
65	
66	```json
67	{
68	  "capabilities": {
69	    "resources": {}
70	  }
71	}
72	```
73	
74	Servers that declare the `resources` capability **MUST** respond to `resources/list`
75	requests with the set of resources currently available to the requesting client. This set
76	**MAY** be empty and **MAY** change over time (see
77	[List Changed Notification](#list-changed-notification)), but **MUST NOT** vary
78	per-connection or as a side effect of other requests on the connection. The set
79	**MAY** vary by the authorization presented on the request — for example, returning
80	only the resources the caller's granted scopes permit — since credentials are
81	per-request input, not connection state.
82	
83	## Protocol Messages
84	
85	### Listing Resources
86	
87	To discover available resources, clients send a `resources/list` request. This operation
88	supports [pagination](/specification/2026-07-28/server/utilities/pagination) and [caching](/specification/2026-07-28/server/utilities/caching).
89	
90	**Request:**
91	
92	```json
93	{
94	  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
95	  "id": 1,
96	  "method": "resources/list",
97	  "params": {
98	    "cursor": "optional-cursor-value"
99	  }
100	}
101	```
102	
103	**Response:**
104	
105	```json
106	{
107	  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
108	  "id": 1,
109	  "result": {
110	    "resultType": "complete",
111	    "resources": [
112	      {
113	        "uri": "file:///project/src/main.rs",
114	        "name": "main.rs",
115	        "title": "Rust Software Application Main File",
116	        "description": "Primary application entry point",
117	        "mimeType": "text/x-rust",
118	        "icons": [
119	          {
120	            "src": "https://example.com/rust-file-icon.png",
121	            "mimeType": "image/png",
122	            "sizes": ["48x48"]
123	          }
124	        ]
125	      }
126	    ],
127	    "nextCursor": "next-page-cursor",
128	    "ttlMs": 300000,
129	    "cacheScope": "public"
130	  }
131	}
132	```
133	
134	### Reading Resources
135	
136	To retrieve resource contents, clients send a `resources/read` request. This operation
137	supports [caching](/specification/2026-07-28/server/utilities/caching).
138	
139	**Request:**
140	
141	```json
142	{
143	  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
144	  "id": 2,
145	  "method": "resources/read",
146	  "params": {
147	    "uri": "file:///project/src/main.rs"
148	  }
149	}
150	```
151	
152	**Response:**
153	
154	```json
155	{
156	  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
157	  "id": 2,
158	  "result": {
159	    "resultType": "complete",
160	    "contents": [
161	      {
162	        "uri": "file:///project/src/main.rs",
163	        "mimeType": "text/x-rust",
164	        "text": "fn main() {\n    println!(\"Hello world!\");\n}"
165	      }
166	    ],
167	    "ttlMs": 60000,
168	    "cacheScope": "private"
169	  }
170	}
171	```
172	
173	Servers **MAY** return multiple resource contents in response to a single
174	`resources/read` request. For example, a server could return the contents of
175	several files when a directory resource is read.
176	
177	Servers **MAY** also respond to `resources/read` with an [`InputRequiredResult`](/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/mrtr#inputrequiredresult) to indicate that additional input is needed before the resource can be read. This follows the [multi round-trip requests](/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/mrtr#multi-round-trip-requests) mechanism. When retrying the request, clients include `inputResponses` and, if provided by the server, `requestState` in the request parameters.
178	
179	Alternatively, if the scheme of `uri` is `https://`, clients may fetch the resource directly from the web. See the [Common URI Schemes section](#https%3A%2F%2F) for more information.
180	
181	### Resource Templates
182	
183	Resource templates allow servers to expose parameterized resources using
184	[URI templates](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6570). Arguments may be
185	auto-completed through [the completion API](/specification/2026-07-28/server/utilities/completion).
186	This operation supports [pagination](/specification/2026-07-28/server/utilities/pagination) and [caching](/specification/2026-07-28/server/utilities/caching).
187	
188	**Request:**
189	
190	```json
191	{
192	  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
193	  "id": 3,
194	  "method": "resources/templates/list",
195	  "params": {
196	    "cursor": "optional-cursor-value"
197	  }
198	}
199	```
200	
201	**Response:**
202	
203	```json
204	{
205	  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
206	  "id": 3,
207	  "result": {
208	    "resultType": "complete",
209	    "resourceTemplates": [
210	      {
211	        "uriTemplate": "file:///{path}",
212	        "name": "Project Files",
213	        "title": "📁 Project Files",
214	        "description": "Access files in the project directory",
215	        "mimeType": "application/octet-stream",
216	        "icons": [
217	          {
218	            "src": "https://example.com/folder-icon.png",
219	            "mimeType": "image/png",
220	            "sizes": ["48x48"]
221	          }
222	        ]
223	      }
224	    ],
225	    "nextCursor": "next-page-cursor",
226	    "ttlMs": 300000,
227	    "cacheScope": "public"
228	  }
229	}
230	```
231	
232	### List Changed Notification
233	
234	When the list of available resources changes, servers that declared the `listChanged`
235	capability **SHOULD** send a notification:
236	
237	```json
238	{
239	  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
240	  "method": "notifications/resources/list_changed"
241	}
242	```
243	
244	### Subscriptions
245	
246	Clients subscribe to change notifications for specific resources by sending a
247	[`subscriptions/listen`][subscriptions-listen] request with the resource URIs listed in
248	`notifications.resourceSubscriptions`. The server delivers
249	`notifications/resources/updated` on the resulting stream whenever a watched resource
250	changes.
251	
252	```json
253	{
254	  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
255	  "method": "notifications/resources/updated",
256	  "params": {
257	    "_meta": { "io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId": 4 },
258	    "uri": "file:///project/src/main.rs"
259	  }
260	}
261	```
262	
263	See [Subscriptions][subscriptions] for the full protocol mechanics (acknowledgment,
264	`subscriptionId` correlation, and cancellation).
265	
266	[subscriptions-listen]: /specification/2026-07-28/schema#subscriptionslistenrequest
267	[subscriptions]: /specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/subscriptions
268	
269	## Message Flow
270	
271	```mermaid
272	sequenceDiagram
273	    participant Client
274	    participant Server
275	
276	    Note over Client,Server: Resource Discovery
277	    Client->>Server: resources/list
278	    Server-->>Client: List of resources
279	
280	    Note over Client,Server: Resource Template Discovery
281	    Client->>Server: resources/templates/list
282	    Server-->>Client: List of resource templates
283	
284	    Note over Client,Server: Resource Access
285	    Client->>Server: resources/read
286	    Server-->>Client: Resource contents
287	
288	    Note over Client,Server: Subscribe to changes
289	    Client->>Server: subscriptions/listen (resourceSubscriptions)
290	    Server--)Client: notifications/subscriptions/acknowledged
291	
292	    Note over Client,Server: Resource updated
293	    Server--)Client: notifications/resources/updated
294	    Client->>Server: resources/read
295	    Server-->>Client: Updated contents
296	```
297	
298	## Data Types
299	
300	### Resource
301	
302	A resource definition includes:
303	
304	- `uri`: Unique identifier for the resource
305	- `name`: The name of the resource.
306	- `title`: Optional human-readable name of the resource for display purposes.
307	- `description`: Optional description
308	- `icons`: Optional array of icons for display in user interfaces
309	- `mimeType`: Optional MIME type
310	- `size`: Optional size in bytes
311	
312	### Resource Contents
313	
314	Resources can contain either text or binary data:
315	
316	#### Text Content
317	
318	```json
319	{
320	  "uri": "file:///example.txt",
321	  "mimeType": "text/plain",
322	  "text": "Resource content"
323	}
324	```
325	
326	#### Binary Content
327	
328	```json
329	{
330	  "uri": "file:///example.png",
331	  "mimeType": "image/png",
332	  "blob": "base64-encoded-data"
333	}
334	```
335	
336	### Annotations
337	
338	Resources, resource templates and content blocks support optional annotations that provide hints to clients about how to use or display the resource:
339	
340	- **`audience`**: An array indicating the intended audience(s) for this resource. Valid values are `"user"` and `"assistant"`. For example, `["user", "assistant"]` indicates content useful for both.
341	- **`priority`**: A number from 0.0 to 1.0 indicating the importance of this resource. A value of 1 means "most important" (effectively required), while 0 means "least important" (entirely optional).
342	- **`lastModified`**: An ISO 8601 formatted timestamp indicating when the resource was last modified (e.g., `"2025-01-12T15:00:58Z"`).
343	
344	Example resource with annotations:
345	
346	```json
347	{
348	  "uri": "file:///project/README.md",
349	  "name": "README.md",
350	  "title": "Project Documentation",
351	  "mimeType": "text/markdown",
352	  "annotations": {
353	    "audience": ["user"],
354	    "priority": 0.8,
355	    "lastModified": "2025-01-12T15:00:58Z"
356	  }
357	}
358	```
359	
360	Clients can use these annotations to:
361	
362	- Filter resources based on their intended audience
363	- Prioritize which resources to include in context
364	- Display modification times or sort by recency
365	
366	## Common URI Schemes
367	
368	The protocol defines several standard URI schemes. This list is not
369	exhaustive—implementations are always free to use additional, custom URI schemes.
370	
371	### https://
372	
373	Used to represent a resource available on the web.
374	
375	Servers **SHOULD** use this scheme only when the client is able to fetch and load the
376	resource directly from the web on its own—that is, it doesn’t need to read the resource
377	via the MCP server.
378	
379	For other use cases, servers **SHOULD** prefer to use another URI scheme, or define a
380	custom one, even if the server will itself be downloading resource contents over the
381	internet.
382	
383	### file://
384	
385	Used to identify resources that behave like a filesystem. However, the resources do not
386	need to map to an actual physical filesystem.
387	
388	MCP servers **MAY** identify file:// resources with an
389	[XDG MIME type](https://specifications.freedesktop.org/shared-mime-info-spec/0.14/ar01s02.html#id-1.3.14),
390	like `inode/directory`, to represent non-regular files (such as directories) that don’t
391	otherwise have a standard MIME type.
392	
393	### git://
394	
395	Git version control integration.
396	
397	### Custom URI Schemes
398	
399	Custom URI schemes **MUST** be in accordance with [RFC3986](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3986),
400	taking the above guidance in to account.
401	
402	## Error Handling
403	
404	If the requested resource does not exist, servers **MUST** return a JSON-RPC error with
405	code `-32602` (Invalid Params). Servers **SHOULD** return `-32603` for internal errors.
406	
407	For backwards compatibility, clients **SHOULD** also accept `-32002` as a
408	resource not found error, as earlier protocol versions used this code.
409	
410	Servers **MUST NOT** return an empty `contents` array for a non-existent resource. An empty array is ambiguous—it could mean the resource exists but has no content, or that it doesn't exist at all.
411	
412	Example error:
413	
414	```json
415	{
416	  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
417	  "id": 5,
418	  "error": {
419	    "code": -32602,
420	    "message": "Resource not found",
421	    "data": {
422	      "uri": "file:///nonexistent.txt"
423	    }
424	  }
425	}
426	```
427	
428	## Security Considerations
429	
430	1. Servers **MUST** validate all resource URIs
431	2. Access controls **SHOULD** be implemented for sensitive resources
432	3. Binary data **MUST** be properly encoded
433	4. Resource permissions **SHOULD** be checked before operations
434	5. Servers **MUST** sanitize file paths to prevent directory traversal attacks
435	   when serving `file://` resources

---
title: Resources
---

<div id="enable-section-numbers" />

The Model Context Protocol (MCP) provides a standardized way for servers to expose
resources to clients. Resources allow servers to share data that provides context to
language models, such as files, database schemas, or application-specific information.
Each resource is uniquely identified by a
[URI](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3986).

<Note>
  For brevity, the request examples on this page omit the `_meta` request
  metadata (`io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion`,
  `io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo`, and
  `io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities`). Every request **MUST** include
  the required `_meta` fields; see
  [`_meta`](/specification/2026-07-28/basic/index#meta).
</Note>

## User Interaction Model

Resources in MCP are designed to be **application-driven**, with host applications
determining how to incorporate context based on their needs.

For example, applications could:

- Expose resources through UI elements for explicit selection, in a tree or list view
- Allow the user to search through and filter available resources
- Implement automatic context inclusion, based on heuristics or the AI model's selection

![Example of resource context picker](/specification/2026-07-28/server/resource-picker.png)

However, implementations are free to expose resources through any interface pattern that
suits their needs—the protocol itself does not mandate any specific user
interaction model.

## Capabilities

Servers that support resources **MUST** declare the `resources` capability:

```json
{
  "capabilities": {
    "resources": {
      "listChanged": true,
      "subscribe": true
    }
  }
}
```

The capability supports two optional features:

- `listChanged`: whether the server will emit notifications when the list of available
  resources changes.
- `subscribe` : whether the server supports resource-specific update notifications
  for resources requested through subscriptions/listen using the resourceSubscriptions
  filter.

Servers may advertise either feature independently, together or neither.

Servers that support neither `listChanged` nor `subscribe` may omit it:

```json
{
  "capabilities": {
    "resources": {}
  }
}
```

Servers that declare the `resources` capability **MUST** respond to `resources/list`
requests with the set of resources currently available to the requesting client. This set
**MAY** be empty and **MAY** change over time (see
[List Changed Notification](#list-changed-notification)), but **MUST NOT** vary
per-connection or as a side effect of other requests on the connection. The set
**MAY** vary by the authorization presented on the request — for example, returning
only the resources the caller's granted scopes permit — since credentials are
per-request input, not connection state.

## Protocol Messages

### Listing Resources

To discover available resources, clients send a `resources/list` request. This operation
supports [pagination](/specification/2026-07-28/server/utilities/pagination) and [caching](/specification/2026-07-28/server/utilities/caching).

**Request:**

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "method": "resources/list",
  "params": {
    "cursor": "optional-cursor-value"
  }
}
```

**Response:**

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "result": {
    "resultType": "complete",
    "resources": [
      {
        "uri": "file:///project/src/main.rs",
        "name": "main.rs",
        "title": "Rust Software Application Main File",
        "description": "Primary application entry point",
        "mimeType": "text/x-rust",
        "icons": [
          {
            "src": "https://example.com/rust-file-icon.png",
            "mimeType": "image/png",
            "sizes": ["48x48"]
          }
        ]
      }
    ],
    "nextCursor": "next-page-cursor",
    "ttlMs": 300000,
    "cacheScope": "public"
  }
}
```

### Reading Resources

To retrieve resource contents, clients send a `resources/read` request. This operation
supports [caching](/specification/2026-07-28/server/utilities/caching).

**Request:**

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 2,
  "method": "resources/read",
  "params": {
    "uri": "file:///project/src/main.rs"
  }
}
```

**Response:**

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 2,
  "result": {
    "resultType": "complete",
    "contents": [
      {
        "uri": "file:///project/src/main.rs",
        "mimeType": "text/x-rust",
        "text": "fn main() {\n    println!(\"Hello world!\");\n}"
      }
    ],
    "ttlMs": 60000,
    "cacheScope": "private"
  }
}
```

Servers **MAY** return multiple resource contents in response to a single
`resources/read` request. For example, a server could return the contents of
several files when a directory resource is read.

Servers **MAY** also respond to `resources/read` with an [`InputRequiredResult`](/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/mrtr#inputrequiredresult) to indicate that additional input is needed before the resource can be read. This follows the [multi round-trip requests](/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/mrtr#multi-round-trip-requests) mechanism. When retrying the request, clients include `inputResponses` and, if provided by the server, `requestState` in the request parameters.

Alternatively, if the scheme of `uri` is `https://`, clients may fetch the resource directly from the web. See the [Common URI Schemes section](#https%3A%2F%2F) for more information.

### Resource Templates

Resource templates allow servers to expose parameterized resources using
[URI templates](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6570). Arguments may be
auto-completed through [the completion API](/specification/2026-07-28/server/utilities/completion).
This operation supports [pagination](/specification/2026-07-28/server/utilities/pagination) and [caching](/specification/2026-07-28/server/utilities/caching).

**Request:**

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 3,
  "method": "resources/templates/list",
  "params": {
    "cursor": "optional-cursor-value"
  }
}
```

**Response:**

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 3,
  "result": {
    "resultType": "complete",
    "resourceTemplates": [
      {
        "uriTemplate": "file:///{path}",
        "name": "Project Files",
        "title": "📁 Project Files",
        "description": "Access files in the project directory",
        "mimeType": "application/octet-stream",
        "icons": [
          {
            "src": "https://example.com/folder-icon.png",
            "mimeType": "image/png",
            "sizes": ["48x48"]
          }
        ]
      }
    ],
    "nextCursor": "next-page-cursor",
    "ttlMs": 300000,
    "cacheScope": "public"
  }
}
```

### List Changed Notification

When the list of available resources changes, servers that declared the `listChanged`
capability **SHOULD** send a notification:

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "method": "notifications/resources/list_changed"
}
```

### Subscriptions

Clients subscribe to change notifications for specific resources by sending a
[`subscriptions/listen`][subscriptions-listen] request with the resource URIs listed in
`notifications.resourceSubscriptions`. The server delivers
`notifications/resources/updated` on the resulting stream whenever a watched resource
changes.

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "method": "notifications/resources/updated",
  "params": {
    "_meta": { "io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId": 4 },
    "uri": "file:///project/src/main.rs"
  }
}
```

See [Subscriptions][subscriptions] for the full protocol mechanics (acknowledgment,
`subscriptionId` correlation, and cancellation).

[subscriptions-listen]: /specification/2026-07-28/schema#subscriptionslistenrequest
[subscriptions]: /specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/subscriptions

## Message Flow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client
    participant Server

    Note over Client,Server: Resource Discovery
    Client->>Server: resources/list
    Server-->>Client: List of resources

    Note over Client,Server: Resource Template Discovery
    Client->>Server: resources/templates/list
    Server-->>Client: List of resource templates

    Note over Client,Server: Resource Access
    Client->>Server: resources/read
    Server-->>Client: Resource contents

    Note over Client,Server: Subscribe to changes
    Client->>Server: subscriptions/listen (resourceSubscriptions)
    Server--)Client: notifications/subscriptions/acknowledged

    Note over Client,Server: Resource updated
    Server--)Client: notifications/resources/updated
    Client->>Server: resources/read
    Server-->>Client: Updated contents
```

## Data Types

### Resource

A resource definition includes:

- `uri`: Unique identifier for the resource
- `name`: The name of the resource.
- `title`: Optional human-readable name of the resource for display purposes.
- `description`: Optional description
- `icons`: Optional array of icons for display in user interfaces
- `mimeType`: Optional MIME type
- `size`: Optional size in bytes

### Resource Contents

Resources can contain either text or binary data:

#### Text Content

```json
{
  "uri": "file:///example.txt",
  "mimeType": "text/plain",
  "text": "Resource content"
}
```

#### Binary Content

```json
{
  "uri": "file:///example.png",
  "mimeType": "image/png",
  "blob": "base64-encoded-data"
}
```

### Annotations

Resources, resource templates and content blocks support optional annotations that provide hints to clients about how to use or display the resource:

- **`audience`**: An array indicating the intended audience(s) for this resource. Valid values are `"user"` and `"assistant"`. For example, `["user", "assistant"]` indicates content useful for both.
- **`priority`**: A number from 0.0 to 1.0 indicating the importance of this resource. A value of 1 means "most important" (effectively required), while 0 means "least important" (entirely optional).
- **`lastModified`**: An ISO 8601 formatted timestamp indicating when the resource was last modified (e.g., `"2025-01-12T15:00:58Z"`).

Example resource with annotations:

```json
{
  "uri": "file:///project/README.md",
  "name": "README.md",
  "title": "Project Documentation",
  "mimeType": "text/markdown",
  "annotations": {
    "audience": ["user"],
    "priority": 0.8,
    "lastModified": "2025-01-12T15:00:58Z"
  }
}
```

Clients can use these annotations to:

- Filter resources based on their intended audience
- Prioritize which resources to include in context
- Display modification times or sort by recency

## Common URI Schemes

The protocol defines several standard URI schemes. This list is not
exhaustive—implementations are always free to use additional, custom URI schemes.

### https://

Used to represent a resource available on the web.

Servers **SHOULD** use this scheme only when the client is able to fetch and load the
resource directly from the web on its own—that is, it doesn’t need to read the resource
via the MCP server.

For other use cases, servers **SHOULD** prefer to use another URI scheme, or define a
custom one, even if the server will itself be downloading resource contents over the
internet.

### file://

Used to identify resources that behave like a filesystem. However, the resources do not
need to map to an actual physical filesystem.

MCP servers **MAY** identify file:// resources with an
[XDG MIME type](https://specifications.freedesktop.org/shared-mime-info-spec/0.14/ar01s02.html#id-1.3.14),
like `inode/directory`, to represent non-regular files (such as directories) that don’t
otherwise have a standard MIME type.

### git://

Git version control integration.

### Custom URI Schemes

Custom URI schemes **MUST** be in accordance with [RFC3986](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3986),
taking the above guidance in to account.

## Error Handling

If the requested resource does not exist, servers **MUST** return a JSON-RPC error with
code `-32602` (Invalid Params). Servers **SHOULD** return `-32603` for internal errors.

For backwards compatibility, clients **SHOULD** also accept `-32002` as a
resource not found error, as earlier protocol versions used this code.

Servers **MUST NOT** return an empty `contents` array for a non-existent resource. An empty array is ambiguous—it could mean the resource exists but has no content, or that it doesn't exist at all.

Example error:

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 5,
  "error": {
    "code": -32602,
    "message": "Resource not found",
    "data": {
      "uri": "file:///nonexistent.txt"
    }
  }
}
```

## Security Considerations

1. Servers **MUST** validate all resource URIs
2. Access controls **SHOULD** be implemented for sensitive resources
3. Binary data **MUST** be properly encoded
4. Resource permissions **SHOULD** be checked before operations
5. Servers **MUST** sanitize file paths to prevent directory traversal attacks
   when serving `file://` resources
